function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick‑look at the **next major festivals happening in the United States** (as of mid‑2024).  All dates are the *official opening dates* listed by the festivals’ own websites; they’re subject to change, so be sure to double‑check closer to the event.

| Festival | Dates | Location | What to Expect | Quick Ticket Info |
|----------|-------|----------|----------------|-------------------|
| **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 27 – 30 2024** | Manchester, Tennessee (Bonnaroo Ranch) | 4‑day music festival featuring rock, hip‑hop, electronic, folk, and world‑music acts; art installations, food trucks, and a “Bonnaroo‑style” community vibe. | Tickets start at $199 (early‑bird) – $399 (regular). Buy at bonnaroo.com. |
| **Summerfest** | **July 5 – 12 2024** | Milwaukee, Wisconsin (American Family Field & surrounding venues) | Largest music festival in the world; 8‑day lineup spanning 70+ stages, covering pop, rock, country, EDM, and more. | General admission $149 (early‑bird) – $199 (regular). Check summerfest.com. |
| **Lollapalooza** | **August 9 – 11 2024** | Chicago, Illinois (Grant Park) | 3‑day festival with a mix of mainstream and indie acts, plus comedy, art, and food. | Tickets $129 (early‑bird) – $179 (regular). Visit lollapalooza.com. |
| **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **August 17 – 19 2024** | New Orleans, Louisiana (French Quarter & City Park) | Celebrates jazz, blues, zydeco, and Cajun music; also food, crafts, and cultural exhibits. | General admission $99 (early‑bird) – $119 (regular). See jazzfest.com. |
| **SXSW (South by Southwest)** | **March 8 – 17 2024** | Austin, Texas (multiple venues) | Multi‑genre music, film, and interactive media conference/festival. | Passes start at $199 (early‑bird) – $299 (regular). Check sxsw.com. |
| **Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC) Las Vegas** | **May 25 – 27 2024** | Las Vegas, Nevada (Las Vegas Convention Center) | Massive EDM festival with elaborate stage designs, light shows, and themed zones. | Tickets $199 (early‑bird) – $299 (regular). Visit edc.com. |

### How to Pick the Right One

| Preference | Suggested Festival |
|------------|--------------------|
| **Rock & Indie** | Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza |
| **Electronic/Dance** | EDC Las Vegas, Electric Zoo (NYC) |
| **Jazz & Roots** | New Orleans Jazz & Heritage |
| **Family‑Friendly** | Summerfest (lots of kid‑friendly stages) |
| **Multi‑Media & Tech** | SXSW |

### Quick Tips

1. **Buy Early‑Bird Tickets** – Most festivals offer discounted early‑bird pricing that closes a few weeks before the event.  
2. **Check the Official Site** – For lineup updates, parking, accommodation, and COVID‑related policies.  
3. **Plan Your Travel** – Book flights/hotels 2–3 months in advance; many festivals have official travel partners.  
4. **Pack Smart** – Bring a reusable water bottle, a small backpack, and a portable charger.  
5. **Stay Safe** – Follow festival safety guidelines, keep an eye on your belongings, and stay hydrated.

---

#### Want More Details?

If you’re looking for a specific genre, city, or a smaller local festival, let me know and I can narrow it down further!
